correctness.rationale: The rank-two multiplication formula gives two independent scalar orthogonality conditions. These force exactly one natural basis vector along e1 and a pairwise-orthogonal basis of its complement; all such bases yield and realize precisely the complete-split graph family. The cut formula |∂W|=w(n−w)−b(t−b), an enlargement argument to w=floor(n/2), and balancing b near t/2 prove the exact Cheeger expression including parity extrema. All steps use real positive definiteness explicitly. Standalone exact checker verifies both bases and all complete-split graph cuts in dimensions 3–10, without being substituted for the proof.

originality.rationale: The precise May 2026 source presents the singular basis-dependent expansion problem as open. The full quantitative spectrum for a rank-two annihilator-free family and its parity-sharp infimum are not given by earlier graph-change/connectedness examples, contemporary rank-one symmetry theory, or the accessible three-dimensional material. Statement implication comparisons are recorded below; the 2017 full text was not accessible and remains a residual priority risk.
residual_risks: 2017 three-dimensional evolution-algebra classification was only partially accessible; it may contain overlapping low-dimensional examples but cannot alone establish or refute the all-n quantitative claim.
A different earlier analysis of orthogonal natural bases in non-perfect evolution algebras may implicitly yield some graph realizations; a comprehensive global priority claim is not made.
Theorems are for the real field only; no inference to arbitrary-field Cheeger spectra is made.

value.rationale: This is an exact all-dimensional structure and invariant computation directly addressing Problem 8.3 of the source paper: all natural-basis graph types, every attainable Cheeger value, parity-dependent sharp minimum, and unbounded max/min ratio. Its nondegenerate (annihilator-zero) status rules out explaining variation via changing connectivity. The two-dimensional square avoids the previously simpler rank-one setting, so the result is not a one-point cheap counterexample.
